text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc dropped to a near 12-month low in pre-market trade on Monday, extending last week's losses as a press report raised fears over its system of "bundling" channels.
The stock was quoted down 6p at 447-1/2 by 0714 GMT, its lowest since last July, though no trading was recorded in the stock.

A report in the Guardian newspaper said a decision by the Independent Television Commission last week in announcing the award of digital terrestrial broadcast licencees, meant the watchdog may rule in favour of letting subscribers buy channels one by one.
That could lead to a cut in the monthly cost of pay TV and may have a negative impact on the smaller, specialist interest channels, the report said.
An ITC review in favour of unbundling the channels may also force operators to invest more in programmes to raise its standards, the report said.
Shares have already dropped from a high of 608p in mid-June amid concerns over the loss of two top executives and an equity stake in terrestrial digital TV.
Last week Soccer Premier League said it was set to demand more money from BSkyB for television rights next year when digital TV is launched, according to one report.
BSkyB was not immediately available for comment.
